messages:
Priya: Heads-up — Enterprise prospect 'Maple' asked for a capacity/runbook for their commit. They expect 2k RPS steady, 12k RPS spike for product launches, and 95th pct latency target <= 300ms. They want pricing for reserved pool + burst credits and an autoscale policy we can operationalize. Can SRE/infra estimates this?
Marcus: Thanks — sending to infra. Quick Q: are these rps figures per region or global? Also what model size are they planning to serve (7B/13B/70B)? Pricing depends a lot on model footprint.
Priya: Global but they prefer multi-AZ with EU + US. Starting with a 13B LLM quantized to 4-bit for cost; may move to 70B for highest quality in canary.
Elena: High-level mapping: for 13B quant 4-bit on our runtime, an NVIDIA A100-80GB can handle ~650 qps for short-context chat (~128 tokens) under continuous batching. So 2k steady -> ~4 A100s (safety x1.2) => recommend 5 reserved GPUs. For 12k burst, we'd need ~19 A100s peak. We shouldn't reserve 19 permanently.
Marcus: So reserved pool of ~6-8 GPUs + burst credit model to scale to 20 when needed?
Elena: Exactly. Proposal: Reserved commit = 8 GPUs in primary region (EU), with cross-region fallback to US to absorb spike. Burst/spot pool can be up to 20 GPUs with autoscale triggers. We also add model-variant fallback to 7B quant for < 99ms degradation instead of failure.
Kai: Autoscale policy sketch: scale by 95th-latency + queue depth. Minimal example config: 
```
policy:
  min_replicas: 4
  reserved_replicas: 8
  max_replicas: 20
  scale_up:
    - metric: request_queue_length
      threshold: 50
      step: +2
    - metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 280
      step: +1
  scale_down:
    - metric: request_queue_length
      threshold: 10
      cooldown: 120s
fallback:
  - model_variant: "13B-quant"
  - model_variant: "7B-quant-fast"
  - route_policy: "region-failover"
```
Kai: Note: reserved_replicas=8 means we keep 8 warm GPUs; min_replicas=4 keeps a safe floor when traffic drops (preserve cold-starts). Burst uses preallocated spot pools with faster attach.
Jamie: Pricing ask from customer: what monthly cost for 8 reserved A100s + ability to burst to 20 for up to 24 hours/mo? Also what's the surcharge for region failover?
Elena: Ballpark numbers (list price style): A100 reserved slot (enterprise rate) ~ $18k/mo per GPU committed; so 8 -> $144k/mo. Burst credits: we price burst at 1.6x on-demand GPU hourly. If they use additional 12 GPUs for 24 hours = 12 * 24 * (on-demand hourly). On-demand assumed $3.5/hr -> burst cost ~ $1,008 for that event * 1.6 = ~$1.6k. Monthly with one big launch ~ $1.6k extra. Add network egress & cross-region penalty ~ flat $2k/mo estimated. Total rough run-rate ~ $148k/mo. This is high-level; finance will give exact quote.
Marcus: Useful. We'll present reserved + burst credit option and an alternate lower-cost plan: 4 reserved GPUs + 100% burst budget for launches (higher latency tail and more risk).
Priya: They also want an operational runbook for POC handoff (SLA, incident flow, preheat). Can we draft a short checklist?
Elena: POC preheat checklist (short):
- Provision reserved_replicas=8 in EU test AZ
- Upload model artifact + quantized weights, verify checksum
- Warm KV cache with representative prompt corpus (sample 10k requests)
- Run simulated traffic: 2k RPS steady + 12k spike for 10 mins, capture p50/p95/p99
- Validate fallback routing to 7B variant and multi-AZ failover in less than 45s
- Confirm telemetry (per-token cost, p95 latency, queue length) streams to Console dashboards
- Run failover drill: kill 2 GPUs, observe autoscale and degrade gracefully
- Security: ensure VPC peering + KMS keys are in place, and SSO for access
Kai: Also adding runbook snippets for ops page: alert triggers (p95>300ms for 5m), burst budget > 70% consumed, spot attach failures > 3 -> page oncall.
ops-bot: Reminder: deploy-bot scheduled canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC for the POC model. Use release tag maple-poc-v1.
Jamie: I'll ask pricing team for firm numbers and prepare a two-option quote (8-reserved vs 4-reserved + burst-heavy). Priya — want to schedule a handoff call with customer this week?
Priya: Yes, propose Thu 14:00 UTC. Marcus/Elena/Kai, can you join for technical handoff?
Marcus: 👍 can join.
Elena: I can.
Kai: I'll be there too.
Priya: Great — I'll send calendar invite and attach this thread runbook. Thanks all.
